# Regia Engine

> Regia Engine is an editor-first game engine for 3D and 2D games, written in Rust. Games are Rust projects; they build for Linux, Windows and Android (macOS builds from source, for testing). The editor and every game can be driven by an AI assistant through Regia's agent protocol and its MCP server (`regia mcp`). Everything runs on the user's own machine: Regia needs no account and sends nothing anywhere on its own. It is free and open source: the engine is under the Mozilla Public License 2.0, the project templates and samples under MIT-0 or CC0, the manual under CC BY 4.0 (source: https://github.com/Regia-Engine/Regia-Engine).

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask llms-txt`; do not edit. llms-full.txt: 3791178 bytes, 388 pages. -->

Paths are relative to the repository root. If you were asked to set Regia up, read `AGENTS.md` first. `llms-full.txt` holds the Start here, User guide, Systems and Agent guide pages in one file.

## User guide

- [Introduction](book/introduction.md): The Regia Engine Manual.
- [Quickstart for a person](book/start/quickstart-human.md): Install the tools, create a project, and run it.
- [Quickstart for an agent](book/start/quickstart-agent.md): Connect to a project and make one call.
- [Crates and imports](book/user-guide/index.md): A quick map of where things live, for when you know what you want and need the `use` line.
- [Quick start: a game in one file](book/user-guide/quick-start.md): `regia::quick` is the shortest path from nothing to something on screen: one crate, one `main.rs`, three functions.
- [Sketch → App → systems → project](book/user-guide/sketch-to-project.md): A Regia Engine game can start as ten lines and grow into a full project.
- [Project structure](book/user-guide/project-structure.md): `regia new "My Game"` writes a Cargo workspace.
- [Display calibration](book/user-guide/display-calibration.md): Regia Engine's look is judged on a good monitor in a dim room.
- [SpaceMouse](book/user-guide/spacemouse.md): Regia Engine's desktop apps (the editor, Tincal, Red-Rouge and any app built on Regia Engine's UI) support 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse devices for 3D viewport navigation and for 2D panes (image views, timelines, lists).
- [Feedback and bug reports](book/user-guide/feedback.md): `regia_framework::feedback` lets a player send feedback from inside the game.
- [Telemetry](book/user-guide/telemetry.md): Regia Engine emits structured telemetry as `tracing` events.
- [Automatic quality detection](book/user-guide/auto-quality.md): A player's first launch should look good and run smoothly without a trip to the options menu.
- [Android](book/user-guide/android.md): Regia Engine runs on Android phones (aarch64, API 29+, Vulkan).
- [Checking your machine with `regia doctor`](book/user-guide/doctor.md): `regia doctor` looks for everything a build needs and prints, for each problem, the command that fixes it.
- [macOS (testing only)](book/user-guide/macos.md): Regia Engine builds and runs its test suite on macOS with Metal.
- [Windows](book/user-guide/windows.md): The v0.2.17 Windows pass exercised Vulkan and DX12 on the owner's a test machine, including native crash capture, deliberate device-loss exit and clean quits; the N150 laptop also had a native pass.
- [Linux](book/user-guide/linux.md): Linux is a development host and a shipping target.
- [Performance overlay](book/user-guide/performance-overlay.md): Every Regia Engine game has a built-in performance overlay.
- [2D: sprites, tilemaps, 2D physics](book/user-guide/2d.md): Regia Engine's 2D toolkit (spec 22 § T2.10 and spec 86) draws sprites from packed atlases, plays sprite-sheet animations, renders Tiled maps, gives you a pixel-perfect orthographic camera and two kinds of 2D physics: a pixel-exact…
- [Animation clip compression](book/user-guide/clip-compression.md): `regia_animation::clip_compress` cooks an `AnimationClip`'s skeletal tracks into a smaller quantised form under an object-space error bound, checked at every key time, the midpoints between keys and a uniform grid (the report shows the…
- [Montages, sync groups and motion warping](book/user-guide/montages.md): A montage is a one-shot action (an attack, a reload, a vault, an emote) that gameplay starts on a character and that plays over the character's anim graph.
- [Inertialized transitions](book/user-guide/inertialization.md): A state-machine transition can cross-fade (the default) or inertialize.
- [Character rigs: twist bones, drivers, pose-space correctives, skeleton profiles](book/user-guide/character-rig.md): Four pieces that make a skinned character hold up at the joints.
- [Morph targets and skinned meshes](book/user-guide/morph-targets.md): Faces, visemes, correctives and a character creator's body sliders are morph targets (blend shapes): per-vertex offsets the renderer adds to a mesh, scaled by a weight per target.
- [Eye gaze and per-instance bind poses](book/user-guide/eyes-and-bind-poses.md): Two components for characters: `Gaze` makes the eyes follow a target with limits and eyelid follow, and `InstanceBindPose` gives one avatar its own proportions over a shared skeleton and clip set.
- [Editor tour](book/start/editor-tour.md): `regia-editor` is a docking editor built on the engine's own ECS: the panels edit the same world data your game runs, and every edit goes through one undo stack.
- [Running and iterating](book/start/running.md): How to run a Regia Engine game during development, read its logs, configure the window, iterate quickly, try it on Android and turn it into a build you can hand to someone.
- [Checking your game with an agent](book/start/first-agent-check.md): This page makes a First Person project, builds and runs it, then checks it from a second terminal through the agent protocol: wait for the game to be ready, assert what is on screen, take a screenshot and quit.
- [The ECS: entities, components, systems](book/fundamentals/ecs.md): Everything in a running Regia Engine game lives in one world organized as an Entity Component System.
- [App, plugins and schedules](book/fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md): An `App` owns one ECS world, the frame schedules and the plugins that configured them.
- [Scenes: entities, levels and prefabs](book/user-guide/scenes.md): A level is a saved scene — a list of entities, each a set of components with values — stored as canonical RON (`.level.ron`).
- [Assets and the cook](book/fundamentals/assets.md): Source assets (glTF models, PNG and JPEG textures, materials, levels, sounds) live in your project's `assets/` folder in neutral, editable formats.
- [Reflection](book/fundamentals/reflection.md): Reflection lets the engine look inside your types at runtime: list a component's fields, read and write them by name, and turn them into text and back.
- [Input](book/user-guide/input.md): `regia_input` turns platform input into two things you use: messages (raw events) and actions (named, mapped inputs).
- [Tutorial: a third-person game](book/tutorials/third-person.md): In this tutorial you build Coin Run, a small third-person game: run and jump around a level, collect every coin, see your progress on a HUD, save and load, test it automatically through the agent protocol, and package it.
- [Tutorial: the arena](book/tutorials/arena.md): `samples/arena` is a first-person arena shooter against AI bots.
- [Build a networked game](book/tutorials/networked-game.md): This tutorial walks through the `net-game` template: a dedicated server and a client of one shared simulation, over encrypted UDP, with client-side prediction, interpolation, lag compensation and lobbies.
- [Tutorial: your first scene](book/tutorials/first-scene.md): Your first project put one box on screen.
- [Tutorial: a game loop with input](book/tutorials/game-loop.md): This tutorial builds Orb Run, the smallest thing that is a game: you move a box around an arena with the keyboard or a gamepad, orbs sit on the floor, touching one collects it, and collecting them all wins.
- [Tutorial: your first baked light](book/tutorials/baked-light.md): Real-time lighting estimates how light bounces around a scene every frame, with a budget of a few milliseconds.
- [Tutorial: your first scene in the editor](book/tutorials/editor-first-scene.md): This tutorial builds a small scene in the editor without writing code: a new project from a template, a ground, two meshes, a sun and a lamp, a save, and a play-in-editor run.
- [Tutorial: your first material graph](book/tutorials/editor-first-material.md): This tutorial builds a material in the editor's Material Graph panel: a tint parameter multiplied by the mesh's vertex color, wired to the surface's base color, compiled, undone and redone, and saved as a `.matgraph.ron`.
- [Tutorial: package a build](book/tutorials/package-a-build.md): This tutorial takes a project from the editor to a package you can hand out: set the version in Project Settings, check the assets, save, close the editor, and let `regia package` show what it would ship before it builds anything.

## Systems

- [Rendering](book/user-guide/rendering.md): The renderer is a forward+ renderer behind `regia_render::RenderPlugin` (added by `DefaultPlugins`).
- [Dynamic resolution](book/user-guide/dynamic-resolution.md): `regia_render::DynResController` chooses an internal render scale in permille (`1000` is native, `500` is half) from GPU time.
- [The default look](book/user-guide/default-look.md): What a frame looks like before a game touches any lighting or post setting, why, and which knobs move it.
- [Lighting, shadows and global illumination](book/systems/lighting.md): Regia Engine lights scenes in physical units: the sun in lux, point lights in lumens, spot lights in candela, the sky in candela per square meter, and the camera exposed in EV100.
- [Gizmos: debug lines and shapes](book/user-guide/gizmos.md): Gizmos are immediate-mode debug drawings: call a method from any system and the line or shape is drawn for that frame.
- [glTF as a named hierarchy and the wireframe view](book/user-guide/gltf-hierarchy.md): For tools that must address the parts of a model by name (Tincal, a turret editor, a socket placer) rather than place a baked prop.
- [Render overrides and surface picks](book/user-guide/render-override-pick.md): Two editor-side tools for asset apps (Tincal engine requests F5 and F7): change how one entity draws without cloning its material, and find the exact surface point under the cursor.
- [Scalar overlay: per-vertex heatmaps and brushes](book/user-guide/scalar-overlay.md): A `ScalarOverlay` component on a mesh entity colors the mesh by one `f32` per vertex through a ramp, drawn unlit over the lit frame.
- [Model map and node report](book/user-guide/model-report.md): An export check for a glTF/GLB, without a GPU: what is in the model, what is bound, and which budget it breaks.
- [Open kit: view Tincal kits](book/user-guide/open-kit.md): The editor opens the vehicle, prop and character kits Tincal exports for modders.
- [Camera shot sequences](book/user-guide/shot-sequences.md): A shot sequence is a camera move stored as data: a path through space, where the camera looks, its field of view and roll, depth of field, and the cuts and fades between shots.
- [Replay playback (ReplaySim)](book/user-guide/replay-sim.md): `regia_framework::replay_sim::ReplaySim` plays a Direct Order 27 `.do27replay` (version 2, 3 or 4) for rendering, camera and VFX work.
- [Rendering a video (render-out)](book/user-guide/render-out.md): Render-out turns the running scene into finished frames: a PNG sequence, or an `ffmpeg` pipe to an FFV1, ProRes 4444 or DNxHR 444 movie, at any size and frame rate with 1x to 4x supersampling.
- [glTF extensions](book/user-guide/gltf-extensions.md): Regia Engine reads these glTF material extensions on import and keeps the rest.
- [Batch thumbnails](book/user-guide/thumbnails.md): `ThumbnailRenderer` renders many small pictures of models or entities through one device and one warm frame renderer.
- [Custom handles and snap targets](book/user-guide/handles.md): For asset tools (Tincal engine request F6): handles beyond translate, rotate and scale, and snapping to the features of a mesh.
- [Skinning: compute path, dual quaternions, eight influences](book/user-guide/skinning.md): By default Regia Engine skins a mesh in each pass's vertex shader (`specs/13` § 8): four joint influences per vertex, linear blending.
- [The Bake panel](book/user-guide/bake-panel.md): The Bake tab (bottom dock, next to Kit) bakes indirect light for a part of the level into a `.fgiv` volume.
- [Post volumes and the physical camera](book/user-guide/post-volumes.md): A post volume changes the look of a place: walk into a cellar and the image warms, opens up a stop and loses a little saturation; walk out and it blends back.
- [Software masked occlusion culling](book/user-guide/masked-occlusion.md): `regia_render::masked_occlusion::MaskedOcclusionCuller` is a CPU occlusion culler for low-end and Android devices, for frames where the GPU Hi-Z path (the depth pyramid and the two-phase prepass) is unavailable or too expensive.
- [Materials, textures and import](book/user-guide/materials.md): Materials are `shader + parameters`, stored as `.material.ron`.
- [Material graphs](book/systems/material-graph.md): A material graph (`.matgraph.ron`) describes a surface as a graph of nodes (texture samples, math, triplanar projection, height blends, Fresnel) instead of fixed parameters.
- [Mask recolor and decal slots](book/user-guide/mask-decals.md): One character, four factions, a number on every chest: `MaskDecals` recolors and decorates a mesh instance at draw time from per-instance values, so there are no per-faction texture bakes, no material clones and no extra draws.
- [Shading models: skin, eye, fabric sheen](book/user-guide/shading-models.md): Character shading for realistic faces and garments (Tincal engine items B3, B4 and B6).
- [Terrain, tunnels and scatter](book/user-guide/terrain-vfx.md): `regia_terrain` provides heightfields rendered with continuous LOD (CDLOD), material layer stacks, layer-driven scattering of rocks and vegetation, and mesh tunnels through the ground.
- [Photoreal terrain](book/user-guide/terrain-photoreal.md): The photoreal material path for `regia_terrain` (`docs/specs/26-terrain-vfx-highend.md`): height-blended layers, triplanar projection, micro-normal detail and whole-map macro variation, over the CDLOD heightfield the simulation agrees with.
- [Terrain data: cooking and streaming](book/user-guide/terrain-data.md): The photoreal terrain DATA path turns a 4096² 16-bit heightfield and 8K macro / 2K–4K layer textures into a streamable, byte-reproducible virtual-texture layout.
- [Volumetric terrain: dual contouring chunks](book/user-guide/volume-mesh.md): `regia_terrain::volume_mesh` meshes signed-distance fields — caves, overhangs, tunnels and other volumes a heightfield cannot express — by dual contouring (Ju, Losasso, Schaefer & Warren, SIGGRAPH 2002).
- [VFX and decals](book/systems/vfx.md): `regia_vfx` provides GPU particles, projected decals, ribbon trails and camera shake.
- [Physics](book/user-guide/physics.md): `regia_physics` is a thin Rust layer over the rapier3d solver, driven by ECS components and synced both ways.
- [Continuous collision detection (CCD queries)](book/systems/physics-ccd.md): `regia_physics::ccd` answers one question without a physics world: two convex shapes move from pose A to pose B over one step — do they touch, and if so, when and where?
- [Animation](book/user-guide/animation.md): `regia_animation` imports glTF clips, plays skeletal animation, and runs anim graphs — state machines, blend spaces and layers that decide what plays.
- [Audio](book/user-guide/audio.md): `regia_audio` is a runtime audio layer over kira, with buses, snapshots, event cues, parametric patches, spatial audio and voice capture.
- [Loudness (EBU R128)](book/user-guide/loudness.md): `regia_audio` measures perceived loudness per EBU R128 / ITU-R BS.1770-4, so you can normalize assets to a consistent level instead of guessing by peak or RMS.
- [Runtime UI](book/user-guide/ui.md): `regia_ui` is the runtime (in-game) UI — HUD, menus, toasts — driven by taffy layout and cosmic-text, behind `UiPlugin` (added by `DefaultPlugins` when the `ui` feature is on).
- [Radial menu (weapon wheel, unit wheel)](book/user-guide/radial-menu.md): `regia_ui::RadialMenu` is a reusable wheel for gamepad stick, mouse and touch: two to twelve sectors, an optional centre action, an icon and a label per sector, hold-to-open or toggle, release-to-select or press-to-select, and an…
- [Game widgets](book/user-guide/game-widgets.md): Most multiplayer and action games need the same few screens.
- [Runtime UI: a tour](book/user-guide/ui-tour.md): Runtime UI shows how to author a HUD.
- [Navigation & AI](book/user-guide/navigation-ai.md): `regia_nav` builds a navmesh from level geometry and moves agents over it with pathfinding and local avoidance.
- [Goal-oriented action planning (GOAP)](book/user-guide/goap.md): `regia_ai::goap` is a planner for agents that choose *what to do next* by chaining actions: give it the actions an agent can perform (each with preconditions, effects and a cost), the world as it is now, and a goal as a partial description…
- [Gameplay: players, characters, rules and save games](book/user-guide/gameplay.md): `regia_framework` is the gameplay layer: players and controllers, characters, game rules, scripts, settings, and save games.
- [Networking and the sim bridge](book/systems/sim-bridge.md): Some games keep their authoritative state outside the engine: a deterministic lockstep or rollback simulation, a server-authoritative model, a simulation written as a separate library and shared with a dedicated server.
- [Snapshot delta codec](book/systems/snapshot-delta.md): `regia_net::snapshot_delta` is a standalone, schema-driven codec for sending world state as quantized snapshots: a full snapshot first, then per-entity deltas against the last snapshot the receiver acknowledged.
- [Look-dev harness](book/user-guide/lookdev.md): `samples/lookdev` is the measured feedback loop for the DO27 alpha maps.
- [Host look checklist](book/user-guide/host-look-checklist.md): The look-dev harness renders DO27's content the way the parity sheets show it (`docs/evidence/parity/2026-10-07/ferrite-do27-sheet.png`, made before the rename).
- [DO27 host checklist](book/user-guide/do27-host-checklist.md): The base frame (Desktop High, the planet sky, the shared terrain draw, exposure, scatter) is Host look checklist.
- [DO27 interface contracts (v0.2.0)](book/user-guide/do27-interface-contract.md): This page names the data and the code that Direct Order 27 builds against for the v0.2.0 tunnels bundle: what DO27's bake writes, what Regia Engine loads and renders, and what each side may rely on.
- [Adopting engine features](book/user-guide/adopting-features.md): This page is for a game that already ships its own code for something Regia Engine now does.
- [Tunnels Stage B: the switch note for DO27](book/user-guide/tunnels-stage-b-switch.md): This page is for Direct Order 27 (DO27), the game that matches Regia Engine's tunnel query bit for bit today.
- [DO27 switch package for v0.7](book/user-guide/do27-switch-v07.md): This page is for Direct Order 27 (DO27), the game that is moving its engine-general code onto Regia Engine.
- [Performance & benches](book/user-guide/perf-benches.md): Every headless or offscreen device goes through `RenderDevice::headless`.
- [The merge gate and goldens across machines](book/user-guide/merge-gate.md): Every merge to `main` passes one gate: `cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, every workspace test, rustdoc with `-D warnings`, the packaging end-to-end test (`package_e2e -- --ignored`), the Khronos glTF samples, and the `xtask` checks…
- [Look CI: the look check at every green tag](book/user-guide/look-ci.md): The merge gate proves a tag builds and its goldens hold.
- [Sky Lab: a day and a change of weather](book/user-guide/sky-lab.md): Sky Lab (`samples/sky_lab`) is a small headless sample for the sky.
- [Editor](book/user-guide/editor.md): The editor (`regia-editor`) is a docking UI over the engine's own ECS: a Viewport, Outliner, Inspector, Content Browser and Output Log, all editing the same world the game runs.
- [Independent viewports](book/user-guide/viewports.md): The editor's main viewport keeps its camera, layout and display settings in three world resources: `EditorCamera`, `ViewportLayout` and `ViewportSettings`.
- [Hot reload](book/user-guide/hot-reload.md): Hot reload recompiles your game crate and swaps it into the running editor without restarting — state survives.
- [Live asset reload](book/user-guide/live-asset-reload.md): Save a file, see it in the running game or editor, no restart.
- [Agent protocol](book/user-guide/agent-protocol.md): Regia Engine's defining feature: every capability a human has in the editor is available to an AI agent through a typed, documented, testable API (`docs/specs/23-agent-native.md`).
- [Packaging](book/user-guide/packaging.md): Packaging cooks your assets, builds the launcher and assembles a distributable.
- [Binary size](book/user-guide/binary-size.md): The executable (or the Android `.so`) is the biggest single file of most games.
- [Steam](book/user-guide/steam.md): `regia_steam` integrates Steamworks, and the CLI stages and uploads Steam builds.
- [Steam Deck](book/user-guide/steam-deck.md): The Deck is a Regia Engine target: a 7" 1280×800 handheld that runs native Linux games in the Steam Linux Runtime (Linux, Steam, Packaging).
- [Steam real run: two accounts, two machines](book/user-guide/steam-real-run.md): One owner session that checks `regia_steam` against a real Steam client (spec 24 § 4).
- [Test bundles for Windows and the Steam Deck](book/user-guide/test-bundles.md): `cargo xtask dist` builds a folder (and a zip or tar of it) that you copy to a Windows PC or a Steam Deck to run engine binaries there, with no Rust toolchain on that machine.
- [Packaging the demo](book/user-guide/demo-package.md): `cargo xtask demo-package` turns the showcase's free-camera demo (`showcase --demo`) into something you can hand out or upload.
- [Profiling and performance tools](book/systems/profiling.md): Regia Engine treats frame time as a feature: per-frame engine work carries `tracing` spans, the GPU passes are timed with timestamp queries, frame statistics are always available to the game and the agent protocol, and soak runs check…
- [Mesh queries](book/systems/mesh-queries.md): `regia_core::mesh_query` answers spatial questions about triangle meshes and point sets on the CPU: where does a ray hit, what is the closest surface point, which triangles are in this box, do two meshes touch, is a point inside, how far…
- [Vehicles](book/user-guide/vehicles.md): `regia_physics::vehicle` drives wheeled vehicles with rapier's ray-cast vehicle controller.
- [Cargo features](book/user-guide/cargo-features.md): Every Cargo feature of the engine crates is listed, with what it does and its guide page, in § 1 of the coverage map; `cargo xtask book-coverage` fails when a crate gains a feature with no row there (book coverage).
- [Accessibility](book/user-guide/accessibility.md): Regia Engine's runtime UI builds an accessibility tree from your widgets, and with the `accesskit` feature it sends that tree to the player's screen reader.
- [Editor guide](book/user-guide/editor-guide/index.md): One page per area of the editor: what it is for, its main actions with their keyboard shortcuts, and the agent method that does each action, so a person and an agent can do the same work.

## Reference

- [Command-line reference](book/reference/cli.md): Regia Engine has three command-line programs: `regia` (the project tool), `regia-editor`, and the repository's `cargo xtask` automation.
- [BC7 block encoder](book/reference/bc7-encoder.md): `regia_asset_pipeline::bc7_encode` is a self-contained BC7 (BPTC unorm) encoder in plain safe Rust — no FFI, no dependencies beyond the pipeline crate's own.
- [Content formats](book/reference/formats.md): Regia Engine's content formats are frozen: a format's serde shape may only change together with a version bump and a registered migrator, and `cargo xtask check-formats` fails the merge gate otherwise (see Changing a content format).
- [Changing a content format](book/changing-a-content-format.md): A project owner who only needs to move files forward runs Content formats: `regia upgrade-project` with no `--write`, then the same command with `--write`.
- [BC6H HDR texture blocks](book/reference/bc6h.md): BC6H compresses HDR textures: 4×4 blocks of linear RGB half floats become 16 bytes (8 bits a texel, the same footprint as BC7 but for `rgba16float`-range content).
- [The ETC2 / EAC block encoder](book/reference/etc2-encoder.md): The `regia_asset_pipeline::etc2_encode` module is the full-mode ETC2 / EAC block encoder for Android GPUs without ASTC (ADR-1379's follow-up).
- [Render profiles and settings](book/reference/render-profiles.md): `RenderSettings` (a resource) holds the active `RenderProfile`, the `PostSettings` and the `FogSettings`.
- [Agent methods](book/reference/agent-methods.md): Every method of the agent protocol (1409 methods), grouped by area, in the order the schema lists them.
- [The pure-Rust ASTC encoder](book/reference/astc-encoder.md): `regia_asset_pipeline::astc_encode` is a dependency-free, safe-Rust ASTC block encoder for LDR textures, written from the Khronos ASTC LDR specification (see `docs/provenance.md`).
- [Coverage map](book/COVERAGE.md): This page maps every crate feature, agent-protocol method, CLI command and content format to the page that documents it.
- [Index](book/reference/index.md): The index lists every term marked in a book page and every H1 and H2 heading.
- [Glossary](book/reference/glossary.md): The glossary defines the words the manual uses for Regia Engine.
- [Feature catalog](book/reference/feature-catalog.md): The feature catalog lists Regia Engine's features by area, with the page, crate and spec for each one.

## Agent guide

- [Driving a running Regia Engine app (agent protocol 0.2)](book/agents/protocol.md): Every dev build of a Regia Engine game (feature `agent`, on by default) runs a small server that lets an AI agent — or a script — inspect and drive it while it runs.
- [Local transport (Unix socket / named pipe)](book/agents/local-transport.md): The agent protocol serves its JSON-RPC 2.0 surface over two transports at once (specs/23 § 2): the loopback WebSocket listener (`ws://127.0.0.1:<random port>`) and a local transport — a Unix domain socket on Linux/macOS, a named pipe on…
- [Scene: finding, inspecting and editing entities](book/agents/scene.md): Find entities with `scene.query_entities`, read them with `scene.get_entity`, edit them with `scene.set_property` (and friends).
- [Assets: what the running app can load](book/agents/assets.md): The runtime asset surface sits on the running [`AssetServer`]: it lists the cooked manifest, reports load state, loads assets into the app and reloads them.
- [Seeing: screenshots, strips and image comparison](book/agents/seeing.md): Everything an agent needs to *see* results: PNG captures of the window or a mesh asset, multi-frame strips, orbit contact sheets, and SSIM comparison with a difference image.
- [Renderer excellence: reference traces and scoring](book/agents/renderer-excellence.md): Regia Engine has a reference path tracer (`regia_pt`, `docs/specs/27-renderer-excellence.md` § 1) that renders the same meshes, materials, lights and sky as the real-time frame, with the same BRDF code, in physical units.
- [Testing gameplay: pause, step, wait_until, expect](book/agents/testing.md): The protocol runs the game deterministically for you: pause, step exact frames, inject input, and verify the world with predicates (`play.wait_until`) and assertions (`play.expect`).
- [Hitches (`play.hitch_report`, the DO27 soak)](book/agents/hitches.md): `specs/27` § 2.4 makes zero hitches a hard gate: after a 2 s warm-up, no pipeline or bind group is created on the frame path, no frame blocks on the GPU, no frame is over 50 ms, at most 0.1 % of frames are over 2 × p50, p99/p50 ≤ 1.3…
- [Instant load (boot splash, pipeline warm-up, load sets, memory budget)](book/agents/instant-load.md): DO27's "feels instant" budget — branding < 1 s, menu interactive < 1 s, Ready → in control < 1 s with no loading screen — is checked through four methods registered as read-only.
- [Low-memory GPUs (agent)](book/agents/low-memory-gpus.md): How an agent checks the out-of-memory handling of a running game: whether the integrated-GPU defaults apply, whether texture streaming caught allocation failures, and what fills GPU memory.
- [Logs and engine events](book/agents/events.md): Two polled streams, both with the same cursor pattern: keep the returned `next` and pass it as `since` on the next call to read only what is new.
- [Crash reports (`diagnostics.crash_reports`)](book/agents/crash-reports.md): When a running app panics, the platform panic hook writes a self-contained crash report to `logs://crash-<timestamp>.txt` (panic message + backtrace, build identity, OS/GPU facts, the active level and frame count, and the last 200 log…
- [Feedback bundles (`feedback.capture`, `feedback.list`)](book/agents/feedback.md): A feedback bundle is one `.zip` in the game's feedback folder (`user://feedback`, for example `~/.local/share/RegiaEngine/<game>/feedback/` on Linux).
- [Telemetry (`telemetry.get_last_summary`)](book/agents/telemetry.md): The engine emits structured `tracing` events, all with targets under `regia::*`: the session header, frame summaries, hitches, GPU errors, render problems and streaming events.
- [Framework: scripts, cameras, settings and the sim bridge](book/agents/framework.md): The gameplay-framework surface (`regia_framework`) is agent-readable through reflection: scripts and their slots, camera rigs, live game settings, and the sim-bridge counters DO27's rule A1 checks.
- [Physics: raycasts, overlaps and closest points](book/agents/physics.md): Query the live physics world — find what a ray hits, who is inside a volume, what is nearest to a point.
- [Animation: animator state and graph parameters](book/agents/animation.md): See what every animated rig is doing and drive its anim graph while the game runs.
- [Inertialized transitions: author, observe, verify](book/agents/inertialization.md): Inertialized transitions are a per-transition `blend` mode of the anim-graph state machine (`Crossfade` | `Inertialize` | `InertializeSpring`, `book/user-guide/inertialization.md`).
- [Spring bones: hair, tails and cloth strips](book/agents/spring-bones.md): Secondary motion for skinned rigs: chains of joints that lag, swing and settle after the animation has posed the body, and are pushed out of body colliders.
- [Character rigs: attach, observe, verify](book/agents/character-rig.md): Twist chains, helper joints, drivers and pose-space correctives (`.drivers.ron`, `docs/formats/drivers-ron.md`, user guide) and skeleton profiles (`.skelprofile.ron`).
- [Morph weights: blend shapes, expression layers, GPU counters](book/agents/morph-weights.md): Read and set the morph (blend shape) weights of a mesh while the game runs, then check the result with a screenshot.
- [Eye gaze and per-instance bind poses: drive and verify](book/agents/eyes-and-bind-poses.md): User guide: `book/user-guide/eyes-and-bind-poses.md`.
- [Navigation: navmesh queries and dynamic obstacles](book/agents/navigation.md): Inspect the navmesh and query paths without driving gameplay.
- [Smart objects: interaction slots agents can discover, claim and use](book/agents/smart-objects.md): A smart object is a world entity that advertises *interaction slots* — places an AI agent (or a player) can stand, sit or operate — so agents can find and use a chair, terminal, door or cover point without bespoke per-object code.
- [Functional tests: place a test in a level, run it, read the verdict](book/agents/functional-tests.md): A functional test is an entity with a `FunctionalTest` component placed in a level.
- [Gizmos: debug overlays](book/agents/gizmos.md): Turn the engine's debug overlays on and off, and restyle any gizmo group, to see what the game cannot show: collider shapes, the nav mesh, audio emitter ranges and AI senses.
- [glTF hierarchy and wireframe](book/agents/gltf-hierarchy.md): Spawns a glTF/GLB as a named entity tree.
- [Render overrides and surface picks](book/agents/render-override-pick.md): Tints, ghosts, x-rays or unlights one entity without touching its material.
- [Scalar overlay (per-vertex heatmaps)](book/agents/scalar-overlay.md): Colors one mesh entity by one number per vertex, drawn unlit over the lit viewport: skin-weight heatmaps, deformation heatmaps, damage brushes.
- [Model map and node report](book/agents/model-report.md): Read-only, CPU only.
- [Open kit](book/agents/open-kit.md): Read-only.
- [Animation robustness: clip reports and playback rules](book/agents/animation-robustness.md): `anim.clip_report` checks the clips a rig plays before they show up as a wrong pose: broken key data, notifies that can never fire, root motion that drifts per lap, and how far the cook's compression moves the joints.
- [Resource inspector: list and dump GPU targets](book/agents/resource-inspector.md): When a frame looks wrong, the useful question is what an intermediate target holds: the HDR color before tonemapping, the depth, the velocity, the ambient-occlusion result, a shadow atlas, the terrain virtual-texture atlas, the cloud…
- [Batch thumbnails](book/agents/thumbnails.md): Many small renders of models or entities in one call, on one warm renderer.
- [Shading models: skin, eye, fabric sheen](book/agents/shading-models.md): Character materials (Tincal B3, B4, B6).
- [Handles and snap targets](book/agents/handles.md): The snap points of an entity subtree.
- [Skinning](book/agents/skinning.md): Skinned meshes are drawn one of two ways.
- [Radial menu](book/agents/radial-menu.md): `regia_ui` has no per-widget protocol methods; an agent drives the wheel through the same input paths a player uses, and reads the result from the wheel's component and its messages.
- [Quick draw: what the immediate layer drew](book/agents/quick-draw.md): Games, prototypes and examples built on `regia_quick` draw every frame through two resources: `Draw` (2D shapes, paths, meshes and text over the frame) and `Draw3d` (lit cubes, spheres, cylinders, cones, planes, grids and lines in the…
- [UI widget style: states, sizes and density](book/agents/ui-widget-style.md): How a `regia_ui` widget decides what it looks like.
- [Quick apps: the model, the loop, and driving a one-file game](book/agents/quick-app.md): A quick app (`regia::quick::app(model).update(update).view(view)`, `examples/quick/*.rs`, projects from `regia new --template quick`) keeps its whole game state in one reflected resource, `regia_quick::app::Model<crate::YourModel>`.
- [Decals: scorch, pad markings, ruts](book/agents/decals.md): Project a prefab onto a hit, lay a strip along a path, or read how many decals the last view kept.
- [Glass: own canopy and damage](book/agents/glass.md): Per-instance glass control for transmissive meshes (`regia_render::glass`).
- [Mask recolor and decal slots](book/agents/mask-decals.md): Per-instance recolor and decals on a mesh (`regia_render::mask_decals`, Tincal B7): one material and one set of textures, many looks.
- [Draw integrity and skinned bounds](book/agents/draw-integrity.md): Two renderer health readings on one page (`FrameRenderer::draw_integrity`, W2.2):
- [Audio: emitters, listeners, reverb, propagation](book/agents/audio.md): Inspect and tune entity sound without code.
- [Audio zones](book/agents/audio-zones.md): Reverb volumes with presets, a per-zone distance scale, rock-thickness occlusion and mouth routing (`docs/specs/16-audio.md` § 3d).
- [Voice capture and loopback](book/agents/voice.md): Inspect and drive the voice capture stream and the voice loopback (specs/16 § 3b).
- [Gameplay: players, possession and save games](book/agents/gameplay.md): The M20 gameplay surface lets an agent see who is playing, switch what a controller drives, and save or restore the running world.
- [Coroutines](book/agents/coroutines.md): Gameplay coroutines (`regia_framework::coroutine`) are `async` sequences — cutscenes, tutorials, spawn waves — polled once per frame.
- [DO27 replay and Moments](book/agents/replay.md): `regia_framework::replay_sim::ReplaySim` plays a Direct Order 27 `.do27replay` (version 2, 3 or 4, `spec/replay/do27-replay-v3.md` in the DO27 repo) for rendering and camera work.
- [Frame loop and quitting](book/agents/loop.md): Control how the running app steps frames, and ask it to quit, without touching game code.
- [Game states: GameFlow, sub-states and computed states](book/agents/states.md): Games built on Regia Engine describe their flow (title screen, loading, play, pause) as game states (`regia_ecs::state`, adopted from `bevy_state`).
- [Arena: driving and verifying the first-person bot arena](book/agents/arena.md): `samples/arena` is a first-person arena shooter against script-driven bots (`docs/specs/14` M20).
- [Safety: permissions, read-only mode, audit and provenance](book/agents/safety.md): The owner stays in control (specs/23 § 5).
- [Editor surface (M10 shell, M11 workflows)](book/agents/editor.md): The M10 editor shell is agent-controllable through the same protocol as the runtime: the `editor.*` methods below are registered by the editor as an extension of the shared method table, so they go through the same permission checks, rate…
- [Reference image (concept ghost)](book/agents/reference-image.md): Draw a picture in a viewport pane to check the model against a concept: behind the scene, over it, as a difference, or as an outline.
- [Editor theme](book/agents/theme.md): The editor paints with one set of theme tokens: the egui chrome (fills, strokes, text, selection), the viewport overlays (grid, selection outline, icons, gizmo axes, audio ranges) and the panel accents (animation canvases, the "unsaved"…
- [Theme panel (editor)](book/agents/ui-theme-panel.md): The editor's Theme tab edits a runtime UI `.theme.ron` (the files described in UI themes).
- [Shots panel (editor)](book/agents/shot-panel.md): The editor's Shots tab is a small curve editor for the shot sequence that is loaded in the app (camera paths and shot sequences).
- [Independent viewports](book/agents/viewports.md): One world can have several viewports open at once: the editor's main viewport, plus any number of `ViewportInstance`s that a tool draws (a review lightbox, a before/after toggle, a side-by-side concept compare, a candidates grid).
- [Headless deterministic capture](book/agents/headless-capture.md): Run any Regia Engine app offscreen (no window, no compositor) with a fixed timestep, step exact frames through the agent protocol, then screenshot.
- [Distance and height fog](book/agents/fog.md): Outdoor haze on the runtime path: fog gets stronger with distance and with depth below a base height.
- [Atmosphere](book/agents/atmosphere.md): Desktop High and Ultra sample a physically based sky.
- [Map look: exposure meter and color grade](book/agents/look.md): Every map can carry its own exposure and grade in `LevelSettings.look` (scene format v3).
- [Exposure and tonemap (agents)](book/agents/exposure.md): The post stack's exposure and tonemap settings (`PostSettings`) are readable and settable on the running app.
- [Lighting option: Balanced or Depth](book/agents/gi-probes.md): Players choose how indirect light (sky light and light bounced off the ground and walls) looks.
- [Baked GI volumes](book/agents/baked-gi.md): A map can ship its indirect light baked by the path tracer: a `.fgiv` volume made by `regia bake-gi` (format: `docs/formats/baked-gi.md`).
- [Emissive lights](book/agents/emissive-lights.md): Emissive trim (unit lights, building and window lights, strips under a hull) lights the surfaces right next to it.
- [Display calibration (agents)](book/agents/display-calibration.md): The player's display calibration (black level, gamma, HDR nits) runs after the tonemap, VFX and UI, on the finished frame.
- [SpaceMouse (agents)](book/agents/spacemouse.md): Desktop apps read 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse devices (any number, merged into one state): on Linux through the `spacenavd` socket when the daemon runs, otherwise (and on Windows) through raw HID.
- [Render profile (agents)](book/agents/render-profile.md): The render profile is the quality tier the renderer runs (`specs/13` § 3): render scale, AA, upscaler, shadows, post.
- [Mesh LOD tiers (agents)](book/agents/mesh-lod-tiers.md): Rigid meshes with a `MeshLodChain` pick a level each frame from their projected size (ADR-208).
- [Auto quality (agents)](book/agents/auto-quality.md): On a first launch the engine picks the quality tier from the GPU, can confirm it with a ~3 s probe of the first scene after the splash (off by default since v0.1.0, ADR-173), and saves it in `GameSettings.graphics`.
- [Performance overlay (agents)](book/agents/perf-overlay.md): The in-game performance overlay (`regia_framework::perf_overlay`, book page Performance overlay) is a top-left panel.
- [Unit triangle budgets (agents)](book/agents/unit-budget.md): DO27 has a frozen triangle table for each unit class.
- [Camera cuts (agents)](book/agents/camera-cuts.md): A frame blends in what earlier frames left: the temporal upscaler's history (TAAU or TSR), the froxel fog's history, the static-screen SSGI/SSR cache, cached shadow cascades and pages, and the auto-exposure meter.
- [Render-out (agents)](book/agents/render-out.md): `render.out_*` renders the running scene to finished frames: any size, any frame rate, supersampled, with the game HUD laid out for the output, to a PNG sequence or (through `ffmpeg`) to an FFV1, ProRes 4444 or DNxHR 444 movie.
- [Camera paths and shot sequences (agents)](book/agents/camera-paths.md): A shot sequence is a camera move written as data: where the camera is, where it looks, its field of view and depth of field, the cuts between shots and the fades at their edges.
- [UI themes (agents)](book/agents/ui-theme.md): A UI theme is a `.theme.ron` file of design tokens: colors, spacing, radius, type scale, sizes, elevation and motion, plus per-widget looks.
- [UI input events and layers (agents)](book/agents/ui-input.md): Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_input"}`.
- [UI accessibility settings and right-to-left layout (agents)](book/agents/ui-accessibility.md): ADR-273 lane 2, ADR-341.
- [UI tweens and the visual transform (agents)](book/agents/ui-animation.md): Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_animation"}`.
- [UI shortcuts (agents)](book/agents/ui-shortcuts.md): Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_shortcuts"}`.
- [UI drag and drop (agents)](book/agents/ui-drag-drop.md): Guide topic: `agent.guide {"topic": "ui_drag_drop"}`.
- [Volumetric fog](book/agents/volumetric-fog.md): Desktop High and Ultra march a froxel grid (Wronski, SIGGRAPH 2014).
- [Volumetric clouds](book/agents/clouds.md): Desktop High and Ultra raymarch one cloud layer on Earth and Mars maps (an airless preset has none).
- [Weather](book/agents/weather.md): The `Weather` resource (`regia_vfx::weather`, ADR-429) drives the volumetric cloud layer: coverage, cloud type, density and wind, plus a precipitation value for games to read.
- [Rain, snow, wet surfaces and the wind near the ground](book/agents/weather-precipitation.md): The weather falls, wets and blows (spec 99, ADR-1847): rain and snow drawn around the camera, surfaces that get wet and collect snow, and a wind near the ground that foliage, grass, rain and snow read.
- [glTF conventions (LOD, sockets, ORM, variants)](book/agents/gltf-conventions.md): The cook path reads `docs/formats/gltf-conventions.md` and writes runtime payloads.
- [Mesh tunnels](book/agents/tunnels.md): A tunnel through a heightfield is three pieces (`regia_terrain::MeshTunnel`):
- [World pick: rays over terrain and layers](book/agents/world-pick.md): `world.pick` casts a ray through the rendered world and reports the nearest surface and the `MapLayer` it belongs to.
- [Exposure zones](book/agents/exposure-zones.md): A box or a capsule that asks the eye for an EV range.
- [Tunnel acceptance scene](book/agents/tunnel-scene.md): A tunnel is several features that have to work as one set: a hole in the terrain, a tube and lip under it, an interior volume, local fog, a headlight with dust, the sky and auto exposure.
- [Terrain scatter (rocks and props)](book/agents/terrain-scatter.md): A map's rocks, rubble and debris come from its `.scatter.ron` (format v2, `docs/formats/terrain.md` § 2): classes, each with weighted glTF meshes, density rules (density map, noise, slope / altitude / layer mask, exclusion paths) and a…
- [Contact shadows (screen-space, sun only)](book/agents/contact-shadows.md): The cascaded sun shadows resolve a few centimeters per texel close to the camera and meters far away, so small casters lose their shadow: a rock seems to float, a tire does not touch the road, a ledge of relief has no dark underside.
- [Translucent shadows (glass, canopies, visors)](book/agents/translucent-shadows.md): Alpha-blended and transmissive meshes cast a partial, tinted shadow instead of none.
- [Reflection occlusion (enclosed surfaces reflect the enclosure)](book/agents/reflection-occlusion.md): The sky and image-based light reach every surface's reflection unless something says they are blocked.
- [Near sun shadow (the first meters of the view)](book/agents/near-sun-shadow.md): The sun's cascaded shadow maps split the view on a ladder from 16 m to 4 km (ADR-061, ADR-140).
- [Terrain editing (sculpt and paint)](book/agents/terrain-editing.md): `terrain.stroke` runs one brush stroke on a terrain: the same brush core the editor's terrain tool uses (`regia_terrain::brush`, ported from Fyrox's brush-stroke processor).
- [Terrain virtual texture](book/agents/terrain-vt.md): The terrain virtual texture caches the photoreal terrain surface in pages of one atlas, baked by the terrain shader's own surface function.
- [Renderer: scale, culling and output](book/agents/renderer.md): The frame path is `FrameRenderer`.
- [High-end lighting](book/agents/high-end-lighting.md): Desktop High and Ultra turn these on.
- [Look-dev compare](book/agents/lookdev.md): After a photoreal merge, render the shot list and diff it against the committed baseline.
- [VFX](book/agents/vfx.md): `.vfx.ron` v7 is the particle asset (`docs/formats/vfx-ron.md`).
- [Entry streak](book/agents/entry-streak.md): `regia_vfx::entry` draws a body entering the atmosphere along a timed track: a bright head, an ionised trail, a long-lived dust and smoke train behind it, shed pieces, and, below 20 km, a dark body with no glow at all.
- [Hard-surface materials](book/agents/hard-surface.md): Hulls and set pieces pick up detail, a clearcoat lobe, brushed-metal anisotropy, specular occlusion, multi-scatter, parallax panel lines, and curvature edge wear from the standard material.
- [Hair cards](book/agents/hair-cards.md): Hair, eyebrows, lashes, fur and foliage drawn as alpha-tested cards get a strand shading model from the standard material: two Kajiya-Kay highlight lobes, light through the strands, a root-to-tip colour and alpha ramp, and an alpha…
- [Material graphs](book/agents/material-graph.md): A material graph (`.matgraph.ron`, format v4, `docs/formats/matgraph-ron.md`) is a node graph that compiles to the forward pass's `material_surface` function.
- [Animation editor](book/agents/animation-editor.md): The editor's animation tooling has three panels — Anim Graph, Clip and Skeleton — and an `editor.anim_*` agent surface that edits the same documents.
- [2D](book/agents/2d.md): Methods for the 2D toolkit (`specs/22` § T2.10, `specs/86`).
- [Steam](book/agents/steam.md): Methods for the shared Steam connection and the Steam Input bridge: all read-only except `steam.set_deck_preset`, which changes the Deck performance preset (permission `play`).
- [Schedule shuffle and ambiguity checks](book/agents/schedule-shuffle.md): Systems that have no `.before`, `.after` or `.chain()` path between them run in an order nobody chose.
- [Baking GI from meshes](book/agents/baked-gi-bake.md): `regia bake-gi` bakes a map's indirect light into a `.fgiv` volume with the reference path tracer (using the volume at runtime: Baked GI volumes).
- [Runtime UI (agents)](book/agents/ui.md): An agent can see and drive the game UI (`regia_ui`) the way a person does: find a node, click it, move focus, type, and wait for a state.

- [Texture-set census (bindless step 2)](book/agents/texture-sets.md): The renderer binds one material group (group 2) per standard material today: the constants and seven textures (base color, normal, ORM, emissive, detail, detail normal, aux) plus the sampler.

- [Upscalers and quality modes (agents)](book/agents/upscalers.md): A TAA frame renders below the display size and a temporal upscaler brings it up to the display.
- [Frame generation (FSR 3)](book/agents/frame-gen.md): Frame generation presents one interpolated frame between every two rendered frames, so the display shows about twice the rendered frame rate.

- [Shadow stability (sun shadows that hold still)](book/agents/shadow-stability.md): A sun shadow should not crawl when the camera turns.

- [Bent normals (indirect light along the open direction)](book/agents/bent-normals.md): Probe light is smooth: a probe a cell away from a corner holds roughly the light of the open room, and interpolation spreads it into creases, the ground under a hull and the base of a wall that the probe grid is too coarse to see.
- [Toolchain doctor (agents)](book/agents/doctor.md): `regia doctor` checks the toolchains a platform needs and prints a fix for each problem.

- [Showcase: a scene directory for filming](book/agents/showcase.md): `samples/showcase` loads a scene directory and runs it as a headless (or windowed) app with the agent protocol on, so a person or an agent can place the camera, take screenshots and write a frame-exact `render.out` sequence of the scene.
- [Streamed forests: scatter on the ECS frame](book/agents/scatter-forest.md): A map's scatter set can hold whole forests (the showcase map places about 190,000 trees over 8 km).
- [Valley mist](book/agents/valley-mist.md): A mist that lies on the terrain: it follows the ground height, pools in hollows, thins on open ground and ridges, drifts, and is lit by the sun through the same froxel fog as everything else (ADR-1394).
- [Water bodies](book/agents/water.md): Streams, rivers, lakes and the sea, drawn by the runtime frame (ADR-1399).
- [FFT ocean](book/agents/water-ocean.md): A wind sea on a plane water body: a directional spectrum, evolved by a compute pass and turned into tiling maps by an inverse FFT.
- [Terrain grass (dense ground cover)](book/agents/terrain-grass.md): A map's grass comes from its `.grass.ron` (format v1, `docs/formats/grass-ron.md`, ADR-1400): classes of grass, each with density rules (the terrain layers it grows on, slope and altitude bands, a density map, patchiness noise, exclusion…
- [Crash effects: from a vehicle crash to a large surface explosion](book/agents/crash-fx.md): `regia_vfx::crash` (ADR-1398, rescaled by ADR-1414) is a crash or impact for any game, sized by one number: the TNT-equivalent yield of its energy release, `yield_t` in tonnes, from 0.05 t (a light vehicle) to 1000 t (1 kt).
- [Crash blast front: the dust wall and the gust line](book/agents/crash-blast-front.md): `regia_vfx::crash` (ADR-1497) gives a crash's blast front one clock: the front is `343 m/s × t` from the crash point `t` seconds after the detonation.
- [Mesh debris and impact sites](book/agents/debris-impact.md): Throw glTF debris from an effect on arcs that are a pure function of the frame number, lay a crater with burnt ground, and swap a hull to its battered variant at the impact frame.
- [Cinematic profile (agents)](book/agents/cinematic.md): `Cinematic` is an offline render profile above Desktop Ultra (v0.2.0, ADR-1403).
- [Cloud types: genera, diffuse light, cirrus](book/agents/cloud-types.md): The volumetric cloud layer (clouds) has four genus presets (ADR-1408, `regia_render::cloud_types`).
- [Terrain late-winter look](book/agents/terrain-late-winter.md): `TerrainGroundLook` (ADR-1408, `regia_terrain::ground_look`) adds to the photoreal terrain what a tiling layer set cannot carry on its own.
- [Low sun: haze colour and sky](book/agents/low-sun.md): With the sun 9–12° above the horizon, the light that reaches the ground has crossed four to six air masses and is orange.
- [Daylight calibration: grey card, cirrus and lit smoke](book/agents/daylight-calibration.md): Outdoor light in the engine is physical: the sun is the atmosphere's transmitted illuminance (lux), the sky is the sky-view table's radiance (cd/m²), and the HDR target holds the same units.
- [Terrain debug views](book/agents/terrain-debug-views.md): Use these views to find out why terrain looks too dark or too bright: which term is wrong (albedo, sun visibility, the sun's angle, the sky light, occlusion), measured on the frame the game actually renders.
- [Montages, sync groups and motion warping: drive and verify](book/agents/montages.md): User guide: `book/user-guide/montages.md`.
- [Navigation: tile cache and crowds](book/agents/navigation-crowds.md): Drive runtime obstacles and crowd steering without touching gameplay code.
- [Lightmap UV atlas (`editor.atlas_generate`)](book/agents/atlas.md): `regia_asset_pipeline::atlas` unwraps a triangle mesh into charts and packs them into one square atlas, for lightmap UVs (UV2).
- [Frame graph and host passes](book/agents/render-graph.md): The frame renderer records its passes in a fixed order (`specs/13` § 5): shadows, light clusters, probes, the depth prepass, culling, ambient occlusion, the forward pass, the screen-space and outdoor passes, temporal upscaling, translucent…
- [Crash fireball: seen size, soot and toroid](book/agents/crash-fireball.md): `regia_vfx::crash::crash_fireball` (ADR-1498) is the fireball layer of a crash (crash effects), sized by the same yield (`yield_t`, TNT-equivalent tonnes).
- [Camera body and the startled bird (agents)](book/agents/camera-body.md): The camera can be a physical actor: a body with a radius and a speed that the world reacts to as it flies past.
- [Forest flythrough](book/agents/forest-flythrough.md): Use these methods to fly a camera through a dense forest: find the trees along a planned path, measure how much room the camera has, carve a corridor where it has too little, and switch on the LOD and sway settings a fast camera needs…
- [Renaming to Regia Engine](book/user-guide/rename-regia.md): The engine was named Ferrite until ADR-1388; it is now Regia Engine.
- [Fibrous cirrus](book/agents/cirrus-fibrous.md): The cirrus sheet (`CirrusSheet`, Cloud types) draws soft fallstreak trails by default (ADR-1470).
- [Crisp cirrus](book/agents/cirrus-crisp.md): A fibrous cirrus sheet (Fibrous cirrus) is drawn once per cloud-march texel and prefiltered over that texel, so its strands are never narrower than about two texels, and its broad warp and bands come from bilinear texture reads.
- [Post volumes and the physical camera (agents)](book/agents/post-volumes.md): A `PostVolume` component changes the post settings of every camera whose eye it reaches.
- [Data tables](book/user-guide/data-tables.md): A data table holds rows of one Rust struct, each row named by a key: weapons, enemy waves, level-up costs, shop prices.
- [Data tables (agents)](book/agents/data-tables.md): A data table is a list of rows of one Rust struct, each row named by a key (`docs/specs/content-data.md` § 3, ADR-1466).
- [Asset registry](book/user-guide/asset-registry.md): The asset registry answers questions about the project's cooked assets without loading any of them: which assets carry a tag, which are textures, what a model depends on, what uses a texture.
- [Asset registry (agents)](book/agents/asset-registry.md): Every cook writes an asset registry next to the manifest: one record per cooked asset with its id, path, cooked type, tags, cooked size and the ids it depends on (read from the cooked headers).
- [Import folder rules](book/user-guide/import-rules.md): `config/import_rules.ron` (v1) gives every source under a path glob the same importer settings without editing each `.meta` — folder-level import policy for a large project.
- [Asset ids for sources not in version control](book/user-guide/asset-ids.md): Every source asset gets a stable id the first time it is cooked; the id is stored in the source's `.meta` sidecar, and levels, materials and paks refer to the asset by it.
- [Import folder rules (agents)](book/agents/import-rules.md): `assets.import_rules` resolves one source's effective import settings — the same resolution the cook keys on — and says which layer set each field: the asset's `.meta` or a rule of the project's `config/import_rules.ron` (see the user…
- [Localization](book/user-guide/localization.md): Regia's UI text comes from Project Fluent files, one directory per locale.
- [Localization (agents)](book/agents/localization.md): ADR-1466, `docs/specs/content-data.md` § 1.
- [Font subsetting](book/agents/font-subset.md): A font file holds far more glyphs than a game draws.
- [Post-effect and LUT references (CPU)](book/agents/post-reference.md): Four CPU reference modules exist so that effect arithmetic can be tested before, and kept honest after, a GPU pass is written (ADR-1482).
- [Cloth and ropes](book/user-guide/cloth.md): `regia_physics::cloth` is a small, deterministic CPU solver for flags, banners, capes, nets and ropes.
- [Cloth and ropes (agents)](book/agents/cloth.md): `physics.cloth_stats` reports the CPU cloth and rope solvers of the running app (`regia_physics::cloth`, see Cloth and ropes).
- [Motion matching: observe, probe, verify](book/agents/motion-matching.md): Motion matching (`book/user-guide/motion-matching.md`) runs on entities with a `regia_animation::motion_matching::MotionMatching` component.
- [Motion matching](book/user-guide/motion-matching.md): Motion matching plays locomotion without a hand-built state machine.
- [Per-vertex ambient occlusion](book/agents/vertex-ao.md): An opaque lab material can read the alpha of its vertex colors as a smooth occlusion factor on its indirect light.
- [Render-out audio (agents)](book/agents/render-out-audio.md): `render.out_start { audio }` writes the game's sound beside the frames: a stereo WAV mixdown of the master output and, optionally, one WAV per bus (stems).
- [Editor tools (`editor.tool_*`, the Tools panel)](book/agents/editor-tools.md): An editor tool is a separate program the editor launches from a manifest: a review queue, a publishing calendar, an asset checker, a settings page.
- [Capability markers](book/agents/capability-markers.md): `agent.hello` lists named markers in `capabilities`, next to `reflection`, `events`, `assets`, `render` and the others.
- [A tiny replay scene to test replay-driven render-outs](book/agents/replay-scene.md): The repository carries a two-second replay in the engine's replay format and a sample project folder around it, so a tool (Red-Rouge) can try `replay.play { start: "render_out" }` followed by `render.out_start` without any game data.
- [AI: state trees](book/agents/state-tree.md): State trees are the second decision model in `regia_ai` next to behavior trees (`regia_ai::state_tree`, ADR-1565).
- [AI: utility reasoners](book/agents/utility-ai.md): Utility AI is the third decision model in `regia_ai` next to behavior trees and state trees (`regia_ai::utility`).
- [AI: perception, attitudes and planning state](book/agents/ai-perception.md): What an agent perceives, why it picked an action and which plan it follows.
- [Squads, attack tokens, formations and the AI tick budget](book/agents/ai-squads.md): This page is about AI at the scale of a whole encounter: agents that act as a group, take turns attacking one target, stand in distinct places, and do not all think on every fixed step.
- [Pre-fractured destruction (agents)](book/agents/fracture.md): The asset pipeline can split a closed triangle mesh into Voronoi chunks ahead of time (destruction level 2: pre-fractured meshes that a game swaps in and throws as debris).
- [World streaming and HLOD](book/agents/world-streaming.md): The data model for large worlds in `regia_scene` (ADR-1566): a grid of streaming cells, the planner that decides which cells to load, the HLOD tree that stands in for distant cells, and the coordinate type for worlds too big for `f32`.

- [Render jobs: render-out driven by a sequence](book/agents/render-jobs.md): A render job describes a whole render in one file: the shot list to play, the takes to write, where each take goes, the cuts and the output settings.

- [Cooked packs](book/user-guide/cooked-packs.md): A shipped Regia Engine game never parses glTF, never decodes PNG or JPEG and never transcodes a texture at runtime.

- [Terrain runtime: named holes and height patches](book/agents/terrain-runtime.md): Gameplay changes the ground while the game runs: a tunnel mouth is blasted open, a roof collapses, a dozer cuts a ramp.

- [Lockstep state snapshots](book/agents/det-state.md): `regia_detsim::state` saves a lockstep simulation's whole state at a tick boundary and loads it back bit-identical, so a run resumed from the snapshot steps to the same per-tick hashes as the run that never stopped.
- [Lockstep desync hash for ECS games](book/agents/desync-hash-ecs.md): A lockstep game whose simulation lives in components and resources gets the per-system desync diagnosis of Lockstep desync hash without writing a fold by hand.
